lines.text: A woodblock printer starts with a plain block of wood.
Then cuts away everything that is not the picture.
An image model works the other way round. It starts with pure static.
To learn, it takes real pictures and buries them in noise, a little at a time, until nothing is left.
Its only job is to look at a noisy picture and guess the noise that was added.
To make a new picture, it starts from fresh static.
It guesses the noise, removes a little, and looks again.
Twenty or fifty small steps later, a wave appears.
A text prompt steers each guess. That is how a sentence becomes a print.
